newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares surge, signs of recovery seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares surge, signs of recovery seen.

text.p: Singapore shares climbed on Monday, led by a surge of interest in blue chips and electronics stocks which set dealers pondering the possibility of a recovery in the Singapore market.
"The market's up quite strongly and the feeling is quite bullish, so I'm wondering if this is the start of something," a dealer with a local institution said.
At the 0430 GMT lunchtime close, the Straits Times Industrials Index had bounced 26.59 to 2,092.80 -- a gain of 1.29 percent on the morning.
Market volume was a brisk 108.9 million shares.
An anlayst with a U.S. brokerage said a blue chip buying programme backed by U.S. funds was buoying the market.
The effect was reflected in the BT-SRI regional index, which leapt 24.95 or 2.47 percent to 1,033.23.
Dealers said the rise was due to strong showings for Jardine Matheson, up US$0.05 at US$6.75, and Hong Kong Land up US$0.09 at US$2.67. Both stocks had hit new highs earlier in the day.
Singapore Airlines shares took off, leading 168 morning gainers. They rose five percent, or Singapore $0.60, to S$13.30 in active trade of 1.8 million units.
